acceptanceCriteria: An evicted pack or sectioned-snapshot mapping is unmapped once no in-flight Index still uses its bytes (for example a reference count or runtime cleanup), never while it is in use.
A long-lived process cycling through more than four snapshots keeps a bounded number of mappings; a maintained test proves the bound and use-after-unmap safety.
The contract is recorded in the owning index-snapshot spec.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from the V1-0938 multi-root MCP lane (suspected, pre-existing).

Observed in code at 79536edd: internal/contextindex/pack_reader.go retainPack (about line 544) and snapshot_sectioned.go retainSectioned (about line 390) delete an evicted mapping from the 4-entry ring cache without unmapping it, and no finalizer or runtime cleanup was found in internal/contextindex (the only Munmap is the failure path in snapshot_sectioned_mmap_unix.go:26). Expected: a long-lived process such as corvint-mcp (now possibly serving several repositories) keeps at most the cached mappings. Actual (inferred, not measured): every evicted mapping keeps its address space until exit. Clean file-backed pages are reclaimable, so RSS impact is unmeasured. Unmapping on eviction may be unsafe while an in-flight Index still references the bytes.
